summary: The e2e fixtures now serve `generalInfo` in the ADR-0047 shape and stub `GET /v1/config/general-information` with `contact.couple` present, and `design-parity-info.spec.ts` measures the six named sections by `data-slot` instead of a block array. Counts are measured this run, never inherited: the baseline was 405 tests / 32 failed / 343 passed / 30 skipped — 30 in this spec plus 2 the task text did not know about; the after is 420 tests / 384 passed / 6 failed / 30 skipped on a plain run, and 387 passed / 0 failed / 3 flaky with `--retries=2`. Every one of those 6, and both of the 2 in the baseline, is the same DS-kit-harness timeout (`e2e/helpers/ds-kit.ts` starts one `python3 -m http.server` per project and the parity specs navigate it concurrently), spread across four parity specs T388 never touched. `design-parity-info.spec.ts` itself is 45/45 green. Two deviations, both forced by the contract rather than chosen: the app renders six sections against the kit's five, and the no-number contact has to be the groom.

acceptance.criterion: `api-mocks.ts` serves `generalInfo` in the ADR-0047 shape on the config response, and mocks `GET /v1/config/general-information` with `contact.couple` present — it is required on that route and composed server-side (ADR-0047 §4, Amendment 2), so a mock that omits it tests a response the API cannot produce.
acceptance.evidence: `e2e/support/api-mocks.ts`: `generalInfoSections()` (six named fields, no `type`, no block `id`, no stored order) is served as `generalInfo` on `weddingConfigAdmin()`; `GENERAL_INFORMATION` spreads it and adds `contact.couple.{bride,groom}`, registered at `page.route('**/v1/config/general-information', ...)`. `goodToKnowBlocks()` is gone — `grep -rn goodToKnow e2e/support/` returns nothing.
acceptance.notes: `contact.couple` is on the read-route fixture only, never on the `GET /v1/config` one: `CreateWeddingConfigDtoGeneralInfoContact` has no `couple` field, because the digest is not stored inside `generalInfo` — the service composes it (§4). Putting it on both would have modelled a response the API does not return either.

acceptance.criterion: The fixture exercises the cases the render actually branches on: a contact with and without a `phoneNumber`, at least one `faq` and one `note` entry with ULID ids and a note `title`, and a `dayLine` with all three variants.
acceptance.evidence: Four contacts, three with a number and one (the groom) without — asserted by `the contacts card opens with the composed couple, and a person with no number gets no call button`: 4 `.contact-row`, 3 `.call-btn`, row 1 has 0 `.call-btn` and one `.contact-id` (email only). Six ULID `faq` entries (`FAQ_ULID_PREFIX`), asserted through the rendered `id="gtk-faq-01JBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB2"`. One `note` with `NOTE_ULID` and a `title`, asserted as the section label. All three `dayLine` variants stored and distinct, with the rendered one asserted against the variant the Europe/Madrid rule selects and the other two asserted absent.
acceptance.notes: Which contact can lack a number is not free: `phoneNumber` is REQUIRED on `CreateWeddingConfigDtoGeneralInfoContactWeddingPlannerInner` and `...ContactGuestInner`, and optional only on `WeddingGeneralInformationDtoContactCoupleBride`. A planner or guest without one would have been an impossible response. See deviations[1].

acceptance.criterion: `design-parity-info.spec.ts` measures the new section against the kit — six named sections in the DS's fixed order, not blocks. Deviations that are the kit's own go to `../wedding-ui-design/contract/FINDINGS.md`, never reported as app defects (ADR-0044).
acceptance.evidence: The spec is rewritten: `DS_DESKTOP_COLUMNS` / `DS_MOBILE_ORDER` name the six `data-slot`s, `renderedSlots()` reads them in reading order (CSS `order` decides the mobile sequence, so DOM order is not what a guest scans), and the desktop test asserts each slot's grid column from `blockOutline`. The kit side is still measured with the same harness (`blockOutline` on `KIT_DESKTOP_ROOT`/`KIT_MOBILE_ROOT`, pinned to 5). New kit finding recorded at `../wedding-ui-design/contract/FINDINGS.md` (commit `3139bfd`, 2026-09-15 ds-missing-spec) for the two things the kit cannot measure: the `note` section and the reshaped contacts card. The two older `ScreenInfo.jsx` findings (9px gift-row label, gift headline / empty state) still stand and are cross-referenced in the spec header rather than re-filed.
acceptance.notes: The spec header enumerates six structural differences and says for each whether it is the app's, the kit's, or the ADR's — the predecessor's own convention, kept.

acceptance.criterion: `pnpm test:e2e` green, or every remaining failure named with its owner. Report the counts you measure, and do not inherit T384's — it measured a tree that could not run this spec.
acceptance.evidence: Measured this run. BEFORE (`pnpm test:e2e`, at HEAD before this commit): `32 failed, 30 skipped, 343 passed (5.0m)`, 405 tests. AFTER (same command): `6 failed, 30 skipped, 384 passed (4.7m)`, 420 tests. AFTER with `--retries=2`: `3 flaky, 30 skipped, 387 passed (4.8m)`, 0 failed, exit 0. `design-parity-info.spec.ts` alone, all five projects: `45 passed (55.3s)`.
acceptance.notes: Not claimed green on the plain command, because it is not. All 6 plain-run failures are one owner and one cause, named here: the DS-kit harness, `e2e/helpers/ds-kit.ts`. Each is a `page.goto`/first-`click` exceeding the 30s test timeout against the per-project `python3 -m http.server`, in design-parity-overview (×2, iPhone SE), design-parity-dashboard (iPhone 14), design-parity-home (Desktop Chrome) and design-parity-info (×2, Desktop Chrome) — four spec files, three of which T388 does not touch. The same flake accounts for the 2 non-info failures already present in the BEFORE run (overview iPhone SE, config iPhone 14), which is why the task text's '30 failures' was 32. `--retries=2` resolves all of them and leaves 3 flaky, none in `design-parity-info.spec.ts`. The 30 skipped are unchanged: six `test.skip`/`test.fixme` declarations × five projects, all pre-existing (seating-plan ×3, design-parity-overview, design-parity-milestones, design-parity-guests).

deviations.from: "six named sections in the DS's fixed order" measured against the kit, i.e. both sides compared section for section.
deviations.to: Five sections compared to the kit; the sixth (`note`) asserted on the app side alone, with the gap recorded as a kit finding.
deviations.reason: `ScreenInfo.jsx` was drawn against ADR-0046's block array and has no `note` slot at all — it draws five. There is nothing on the kit side to measure the sixth against, and inventing a counterpart would have made the parity spec assert the app against itself.
deviations.authorized_by: T388 acceptance bullet 3 ("Deviations that are the kit's own go to FINDINGS.md, never reported as app defects") and hub ADR-0044 §1 (the DS proposes, SPEC.md decides).
deviations.verified_how: `blockOutline(kitPage, KIT_DESKTOP_ROOT).length` is 5 on every run and the spec pins it to the literal 5, so the day the kit grows a sixth section this assertion fails loudly instead of drifting. Read `ScreenInfo.jsx:187-218`: the wide branch renders dressCode, contacts, gift, faq, venueNote and nothing else. Recorded at `wedding-ui-design/contract/FINDINGS.md` (commit `3139bfd`).

deviations.from: "a contact with and without a `phoneNumber`" read as free choice of which contact.
deviations.to: The groom is the contact without one; the wedding planner and the guest both have one.
deviations.reason: The contract does not allow the alternative. `phoneNumber` is required on a `weddingPlanner` entry and on a `guest` entry and optional only on the composed couple digest, so a planner or guest without a number is a response `wedding-api` cannot produce — the same class of untestable fixture the `contact.couple` bullet exists to prevent.
deviations.authorized_by: T388 acceptance bullet 1's own reasoning ("a mock that omits it tests a response the API cannot produce"), applied to the same field one level down.
deviations.verified_how: Read the generated models: `create-wedding-config-dto-general-info-contact-wedding-planner-inner.ts` and `...-guest-inner.ts` declare `phoneNumber: string`; `wedding-general-information-dto-contact-couple-bride.ts` declares `phoneNumber?: string`. The render's own doc comment (`good-to-know.ts`, the `ContactRow` interface) had already reached the same conclusion independently.

risks.risk: `e2e/public-surface.spec.ts` still asserts the PUBLIC config response has no `goodToKnow` key (line 84) and still poisons it with `goodToKnow: POISONED_BLOCKS` (line 103) to prove nothing renders before sign-in. Both still pass, and both now name an attribute that no longer exists: ADR-0047 renamed it `generalInfo`, and the section reads a separate authenticated route rather than the config document, so poisoning `goodToKnow` proves strictly less than it did. Deliberately not fixed here — T385 owns that file's edits and must invert an assertion in it anyway, and touching it from T388 would have hidden T385's change inside a fixture commit.
risks.surfaces_at: T385, whose acceptance already requires extending `e2e/public-surface.spec.ts` for `couple`/email/phone on unauthenticated routes.

risks.risk: The DS-kit parity harness is load-sensitive and now flakes visibly. `e2e/helpers/ds-kit.ts` starts one `python3 -m http.server` per project and every parity spec opens a second page against it while Babel-standalone compiles the whole kit in-browser; under five parallel workers a 30s test timeout is reachable. Six timeouts on a plain run, three surviving `--retries=2`, across specs owned by four different tasks. Nothing in `playwright.config.ts` sets retries outside CI, so hard rule 11's gate is a coin-flip on a loaded machine — every future task in this repo inherits an intermittently red gate it did not cause, and will spend time proving that.
risks.surfaces_at: Any task that must report hard rule 11 green — T385 next. Candidate fixes: retries outside CI, one shared kit server across projects, or a longer timeout on kit navigation.

risks.risk: `design-parity-info.spec.ts`'s day-line test derives the expected variant from `CONFIG_DATES` with the same Europe/Madrid rule the component uses, so it follows the calendar instead of pinning a string — but it does re-implement that rule in the spec. If ADR-0046 §4's boundary semantics ever change (today the comparison is `<=` on both edges), the component and the spec must change together or the spec will agree with a bug.
